root_cause.text: In f2fs_fill_super(), the positive return value of f2fs_recover_fsync_data() (indicating the number of recovered fsync data items) was not converted to zero for read-only mounts (e.g., ro,norecovery or ro,disable_roll_forward), causing an invalid positive error code to be returned to vfs_get_tree(), which triggered a kernel BUG.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "The root cause is we missed to handle error number returned from f2fs_recover_fsync_data() when mounting image w/ ro,norecovery or ro,disable_roll_forward mount option, result in returning a positive error number to vfs_get_tree(), fix it." The patch diff changes the condition from `if (!f2fs_readonly(sb) && err > 0)` to a nested check that sets `err = 0` for read-only mounts when `err > 0`, confirming the fix.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix mount failure on read-only f2fs by properly handling fsync recovery positive return value: drop recovered data and succeed instead of leaving an invalid positive error code.
intent_record.what: Restructured condition for handling fsync recovery result: when err > 0, check if filesystem is read-only; if read-only, log 'drop all fsynced data', set err = 0; otherwise, keep previous behavior (error out).
intent_record.how: Prevents mount failure on read-only mounts when fsync recovery returns a positive count (indicating recovered inodes). Previously, the positive err would propagate, likely causing mount to fail or return an invalid error code. Now, for read-only mounts, the recovered data are dropped and mount succeeds.

candidates.rationale: This statement assigns the return value of f2fs_recover_fsync_data() to err, which can be a positive number indicating recovered fsync data items. For read-only mounts, this positive value is not converted to zero, causing an invalid positive error code to be returned to vfs_get_tree() and triggering a kernel BUG.
